task.title: Stay Safe on Wi-Fi Networks
task.shortdesc: Follow these recommendations to stay safe on Wi-Fi networks.

step.cmd: Use a trusted Virtual Private Network (VPN) when connecting to public Wi-Fi.

info.p: A VPN encrypts your internet connection, making it much harder for hackers to intercept your data.

step.cmd: Enable multi-factor authentication (MFA) on important accounts, such as email and banking.

info.p: This adds an extra layer of protection, even if your password is compromised.

step.cmd: Avoid logging into sensitive accounts or making online purchases while connected to public Wi-Fi.

info.p: Wait until you are on a trusted, secure network before completing sensitive transactions.

step.cmd: Ensure the websites you visit use HTTPS rather than HTTP.

info.p: A padlock symbol in the address bar also indicates a secure connection.

step.cmd: Turn off file-sharing and printer-sharing features in your system settings while on public Wi-Fi.

info.p: Public networks make it easier for others to access your device if sharing features are left enabled.

step.cmd: Disable the auto-connect feature for Wi-Fi networks on your device.

info.p: Most devices automatically connect to available Wi-Fi networks by default. Turning this feature off prevents your device from connecting to insecure or rogue networks without your knowledge.

step.cmd: Keep your operating system, browser, and security software up to date.

info.p: Software updates often contain security patches that protect against newly discovered threats.

NC State Cybersecurity Training is required for all employees and new undergraduate students beginning in October 2026. It is highly encouraged for all students, staff, and faculty to complete the training to educate themselves on cybersecurity issues.
